key_insight: DreamLite demonstrates that a compact (0.39B) unified diffusion model can run on-device and perform both text-to-image generation and text-guided image editing with competitive quality and low latency.
problem_solved: Large-scale diffusion models are resource intensive and hard to deploy on edge devices, while existing on-device diffusion work focuses mainly on generation and lacks integrated image editing capability.
method: Design a lightweight diffusion backbone and parameter-efficient conditioning so one model supports both T2I generation and text-guided editing.
Train a unified objective that shares weights across generation and editing tasks, enabling consistent semantics and transfer between tasks.
Apply on-device optimizations (distillation, quantization-aware training, efficient attention/FFN blocks and runtime tuning) to meet memory and latency constraints.
impact: Makes high-quality image generation and interactive editing feasible on mobile and edge devices, improving privacy, responsiveness, and deployment cost for AI-powered creative tools.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing the compact diffusion backbone, conditioning pathway for text and image inputs, and size (0.39B) annotation.
Before/after image strip demonstrating text-guided edits (input photo → edited output) alongside T2I sample outputs.
Bar chart comparing model size, latency, and image quality (e.g., FID/LPIPS) for DreamLite vs. large-server models and prior on-device baselines.
Pipeline flowchart contrasting the unified inference path for generation vs. editing (text → sample vs. text+image → edited sample).
paper_title: DreamLite: A Lightweight On-Device Unified Model for Image Generation and Editing
paper_authors: Kailai Feng, Yuxiang Wei, Bo Chen, Yang Pan, Hu Ye
